entries.content_plain:
Introduction

 Rehoboam raises an array, purposing to reduce the ten tribes; but is prevented by Shemaiah the prophet, 2Chr 11:1-4 . He builds several cities of defense, and fortifies others, 2Chr 11:5-12 . The priests and Levites being turned out by Jeroboam, come to Rehoboam, 2Chr 11:13 , 2Chr 11:14 . Jeroboam's gross idolatry, 2Chr 11:15 . The pious of the land join with Judah, and strengthen the kingdom of Rehoboam, 2Chr 11:16 , 2Chr 11:17 . His wives, concubines, and numerous issue, 2Chr 11:18-21 . He places his own sons for governors in the different provinces, 2Chr 11:22 , 2Chr 11:23 . 

 Verse 1 

 Gathered of the house of Judah - See this account 1Kgs 12:21-24 (note), and the notes there.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 5</hi> <div eID="gen14133" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14134" type="x-p"/> And built cities for defense in Judah - He was obliged to strengthen his frontiers against the encroachments of the men of Israel; and Jeroboam did the same thing on his part to prevent the inroads of Judah. entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 15</hi> <div eID="gen14136" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14137" type="x-p"/> And he ordained him priests - for the devils - שעירים seirim, the hairy ones; probably goats: for as the golden calves, or oxen, were in imitation of the Egyptian ox-god, Apis; so they no doubt paid Divine honors to the goat, which we know was an object of religious veneration in Egypt.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 16</hi> <div eID="gen14137" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14138" type="x-p"/> Such as set their hearts to seek the Lord - All the truly pious joined him out of every tribe, and the whole tribe of Levi, being deprived of their functions, joined him also. Thus he had Judah, Benjamin, and Levi, and probably a part of Simeon; for he had Etam, which was in that tribe, and the truly religious out of all the other tribes, for they could not bear Jeroboam's idolatry.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 20</hi> <div eID="gen14140" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14141" type="x-p"/> Maachah the daughter of Absalom - See the note on <reference osisRef="1Kgs.15.10">1Kgs 15:10</reference>. She is called Michaiah, the daughter of Uriel, <reference osisRef="2Chr.13.2">2Chr 13:2</reference>. For this the Targum gives the following reason: "Abijah reigned three years in Jerusalem; and his mother's name was Michaiah, daughter of Uriel of Gibeatha. She is the same as Michah, the daughter of Absalom; but, because she was an upright woman, her name was changed into the more excellent name Michaiah, and her fathers name into that of Uriel of Gibeatha, that the name of Absalom might not be remembered.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 21</hi> <div eID="gen14141" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14142" type="x-p"/> Eighteen wives and threescore concubines - Bad enough, but not so abandoned as his father. Of these marriages and concubinage the issue was twenty-eight sons and sixty daughters; eighty-eight children in the whole, to the education of the whole of whom he could pay but little attention. Numerous families are often neglected; and children by different women, must be yet in a worse state.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 22</hi> <div eID="gen14142" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14143" type="x-p"/> Made Abijah - the chief - Abijah certainly was not the first-born of Rehoboam; but as he loved Maachah more than any of his wives, so he preferred her son, probably through his mother's influence. In <reference osisRef="Deu.21.16">Deu 21:16</reference>, this sort of preference is forbidden; but Rehoboam had a sort of precedent in the preference shown by David to Solomon.

entries.content_osis: <hi type="bold">Verse 23</hi> <div eID="gen14143" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14144" type="x-p"/> He dealt wisely - It was true policy to disperse his own sons through the different provinces who were not likely to form any league with Jeroboam against their father. <div eID="gen14144" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen14145" type="x-p"/> He desired many wives - He was much addicted to women; yet we do not find that he formed any heathenish alliances of this nature. And as no particulars are given, we do not know how far he indulged himself in this propensity. He probably strengthened his political connections by these means.  <chapter eID="2Chr.11"/> <div eID="gen14145" type="x-p"/>
